Risk Premia: Final Research Dashboard

Five commodity asset classes, five sleeves each (Momentum, Carry, Carry-Momentum, Value, Skewness), combined by Equal Weight and Inverse Vol only. Log-return methodology, 5 bps costs, reporting from 2012-01-01 in three periods (P1 2012-2016, P2 2017-2021, P3 2022 onwards) plus a 2026 year-to-date column. All price data through 2026-09-23.
How to use this dashboard
  • Tabs across the top: one per asset class, plus By Style, Cross-Pair, Correlations and Notes (methods and data).
  • Blue filter bars mark every control you can change: period, commodity, metric, Energy with or without NatGas.
  • Tables show IR for every period; click a period heading (or use the filter) to see that period's return, volatility and maximum drawdown.
  • Charts: tick or untick strategies above the chart, change the start period, and hover over the lines for values.
  • Each asset-class tab also has a by-product table (with each commodity's Equal Weight portfolio) and a cumulative-return chart for any single commodity.

Method, data and what changed

Timing convention (all five sleeves)

  • 1-day lag: every signal is generated from closing prices on day t. The position is taken at the close of day t+1 and earns the return from that close onward, so a signal never trades on the price it was computed from. Formally, the position held over day t is wt = st−2, where s is the sleeve's signal, and it earns that day's log return, ln(Pt/Pt−1). Transaction costs are charged when the position changes.

Sleeves (per product)

  • Momentum: average of the signs of three moving-average crossovers, (1,20), (5,60), (20,250), on the raw front-month price.
    $$s_t=\tfrac13\sum_{(a,b)}\operatorname{sign}\!\big(\mathrm{MA}_a(P)_t-\mathrm{MA}_b(P)_t\big),\quad (a,b)\in\{(1,20),(5,60),(20,250)\}$$
  • Carry (V2): For each tenor pair, the carry slope (near - far) / near is standardised against its own trailing 252-day mean and standard deviation. The two z-scores are summed and the sign of the sum is the signal. The position is flat only when the sum is exactly zero. If a z-score is missing, the previous signal is carried forward.
    $$c^{(k)}_t=\frac{P^{\mathrm{near},k}_t-P^{\mathrm{far},k}_t}{P^{\mathrm{near},k}_t},\qquad z^{(k)}_t=\frac{c^{(k)}_t-\mu^{252}_t\!\big(c^{(k)}\big)}{\sigma^{252}_t\!\big(c^{(k)}\big)}$$$$s_t=\operatorname{sign}\!\Big(\sum_k z^{(k)}_t\Big)$$
  • Carry-Momentum (V3): change of the carry slope over 20 observations, summed across the tenor pairs (raw changes, not standardised) and signed; if a pair is missing the last signal is kept.
    $$s_t=\operatorname{sign}\!\Big(\sum_k\big(c^{(k)}_t-c^{(k)}_{t-20}\big)\Big)$$
  • Value: F3 price against its own 1,260-day average, long below -10%, short above +10%.
    $$d_t=\frac{P^{F3}_t}{\frac1{1260}\sum_{i=0}^{1259}P^{F3}_{t-i}}-1,\qquad s_t=+1\;\text{if }d_t<-10\%,\;\;-1\;\text{if }d_t>+10\%,\;\;0\;\text{otherwise}$$
  • Skewness: minus the skewness of the product's daily log returns (roll-adjusted series) over the past 252 observations; long when negative, short when positive (after Fernandez-Perez, Fuertes and Miffre 2021, time-series version).
    $$\hat\gamma_t=\frac{\frac1{252}\sum_{i=0}^{251}(r_{t-i}-\bar r)^3}{\Big(\frac1{252}\sum_{i=0}^{251}(r_{t-i}-\bar r)^2\Big)^{3/2}},\qquad s_t=-\operatorname{sign}(\hat\gamma_t)$$

Tenor pairs (Carry and Carry-Momentum)

  • Metals and Energy: F1-F3 and F1-F13. NGL: F2-F4 and F2-F14.
  • Precious: F1-F2 plus a long pair about 12 months out: Gold F1-F7, Silver F1-F6, Platinum F1-F5, Palladium F1-F5.
  • Agriculture: F1-F2 plus a long pair about 12 months out: Corn F1-F6, Wheat F1-F6, Soybean F1-F8, Soybean Oil F1-F8 (10 to 11 months, the deepest column in the file), Coffee F1-F6, Sugar F1-F5.

Rolling

  • Each contract is rolled on the 5th trading day of the month in which its last trade date falls. The series is bridged on the day after the last trade date, when the data's F1 switches contract. This rolls roughly 14 to 16 trading days before expiry for Energy, NGL, Precious and Sugar, about 6 for Metals and about 5 for Corn, Wheat and Soybeans.

How things are combined

  • Products inside a sleeve are equally weighted on common dates (a dropped date's move is carried into the next shared date).
  • Each asset-class portfolio combines its five sleeves by EW PORT (equal weight) or Inverse Vol (weights from each sleeve's trailing 63-day volatility, recomputed daily).
  • Combined books are two-stage: sleeves into an asset-class portfolio, then the five asset-class portfolios into one book; all four EW / Inverse Vol pairs are shown, with and without NatGas. Cross-pair portfolios blend two asset classes' portfolios the same way. Series are aligned on common dates before weighting.

Data and calendars

  • Prices run through 2026-09-23 for all five asset classes. Reporting starts 2012-01-01; the 2026 year-to-date column covers 1 January to 23 September. Value requires two years of F3 price history before its first signal.
  • Roll calendars: Expiry dates for Precious and Agriculture are taken from Bloomberg and follow its contract-month chain. Metals, Energy and NGL use expiry dates published by the exchange.

Regimes

  • Reporting periods: P1 covers 1 January 2012 to 31 December 2016, P2 covers 1 January 2017 to 31 December 2021, and P3 covers 1 January 2022 to 23 September 2026 (the last price date). The periods are consecutive and do not overlap. The 2026 year-to-date column falls within P3. Each period's statistics are computed on that period alone: return and volatility are annualised over the period, and maximum drawdown is measured from the period's start.
